name: Lenomorelin (Ghrelin)
lead: Ghrelin, whose international nonproprietary name is lenomorelin, is a 28-amino-acid peptide hormone made mainly by enteroendocrine cells of the stomach. It is widely called the "hunger hormone" because it raises the drive to eat, and it also stimulates growth hormone release from the pituitary, which gave it its name.[1]

Its relevance to appearance runs through body composition. Appetite sets how much people eat while cutting or bulking, and growth hormone influences fat and lean mass, so ghrelin sits where hunger, sleep, meal timing and growth hormone meet; people trying to lean out or gain size often describe hunger as the main obstacle, and ghrelin is one of the signals behind it.[1][13][14][34] In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums the hormone itself is rarely used; the talk is about food choices said to move it, and about ghrelin-mimicking growth hormone secretagogue compounds.[2][26][31]

Ghrelin was identified in 1999 as the natural ligand of the growth hormone secretagogue receptor.[1][2] Administered ghrelin has been studied in clinical settings such as cancer cachexia, frailty and cystic fibrosis rather than as a cosmetic agent, and a synthetic ghrelin-receptor agonist, macimorelin, is FDA approved as an oral diagnostic for adult growth hormone deficiency.[3][4][5][15]

sections.h: Use in appearance and physique discussions
paras: Ghrelin enters looksmaxxing and fitness conversation in three ways: as the reason dieting is hard, as a target of food and lifestyle choices, and as the pathway behind a family of growth hormone secretagogue compounds.

Dieters point to the rise in hunger that follows weight loss. A New England Journal of Medicine study of 50 overweight or obese patients on a 10-week very-low-energy diet reported that changes in appetite-related hormones persisted for a year, and consumer-health coverage notes that ghrelin often rises after weight loss while adding that ghrelin changes alone do not reliably predict regain.[10][34]

T Nation posters say eggs and high-protein or fatty meals keep them full and describe eggs as affecting ghrelin; one post quotes the idea that eggs suppress plasma ghrelin, and another recommends psyllium fibre as controlling ghrelin and peptide YY.[26][27] Consumer-health writing likewise says fibre- and protein-rich food may lower ghrelin and that acute exercise appears to suppress it while long-term training may raise it, citing a 2021 review.[34] Forum members disagree about the direction of ghrelin's effect, with some writing that it suppresses hunger; research and encyclopedias describe it as appetite-stimulating.[1][26]

Sleep is the lifestyle lever with the most direct trial support: short sleep has been associated with higher ghrelin and hunger in a randomised crossover study and a 2020 meta-analysis.[13][17] Meal timing studies add that late eating increased hunger in a controlled trial.[14] A 2020 meta-analysis of randomised trials found that skipping breakfast reduced body weight modestly compared with eating it, without a significant difference in body-fat percentage; the abstract does not address ghrelin directly.[32]

subs.h: Ghrelin mimics and growth hormone secretagogues
paras: Wikipedia groups ghrelin with other growth hormone secretagogues: ghrelin-receptor agonists such as the GHRP peptides, ipamorelin, anamorelin, capromorelin, ibutamoren and macimorelin, and separate growth hormone-releasing hormone agonists such as CJC-1295 and sermorelin.[2] Many of these also raise IGF-1, prolactin and cortisol.[2] Their main clinical use is in growth hormone deficiency.[2]

On T Nation, users discuss ghrelin-mimicking compounds taken for growth hormone effects. One poster describes a supplement that mimics the hunger hormone ghrelin and stimulates growth hormone secretion without binding androgen receptors; another says such a product causes 'ghrelin surges' with strong hunger in the first days and noticeable water and muscle fullness.[30][31] A separate thread debates how GHRH analogs and ghrelin analogs differ in mechanism.[29] These are forum accounts; this article does not describe dosing or sourcing.

A T Nation poster in a 2025 thread on semaglutide says GLP-1 drugs suppress ghrelin and other appetite-regulating hormones and that these hormones often rebound after stopping.[28] That is a forum claim; the studies cited elsewhere in this article address ghrelin after diets and surgery rather than GLP-1 therapy.

sections.h: Role in appetite and body weight
paras: Blood levels peak before meals and fall after eating, and stomach expression rises with fasting [1][8]. Ghrelin acts on hypothalamic neurons, including neuropeptide Y and AgRP neurons, to increase food intake and foraging behaviour, and it is linked to reward pathways involved in food and alcohol [1]. A 2007 review describes leptin as the long-term regulator of energy balance and ghrelin as a fast-acting hormone that appears to play a role in starting meals [16]. Reviews describe ghrelin as raising how often meals occur rather than how large they are.[1] A review on ghrelin and blood glucose describes links between the hormone and glucose regulation.[35]

Levels are lower in obesity and after gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy, and higher in anorexia nervosa, Prader-Willi syndrome and cancer cachexia [1][9]. A New England Journal of Medicine study of 50 overweight or obese patients on a 10-week very-low-energy diet reported that hormonal adaptations to weight loss, including changes in appetite-related hormones, persisted for a year [10].

In a randomized crossover study of 12 healthy young men, partial sleep curtailment was associated with lower leptin, higher ghrelin and increased hunger and appetite [17]. A 2020 meta-analysis of 21 studies with 2250 participants found ghrelin higher in short sleepers (standardised mean difference 0.14) [13]. A randomized crossover trial found that eating late, with intake, activity, sleep and light held constant, increased hunger and decreased energy expenditure in adults with overweight or obesity [14].

Ghrelin acts on GHS-R1a, found in the hypothalamus, pituitary, vagus nerve and gastrointestinal tract, mediating growth hormone release, hunger, glucose and lipid metabolism and gut motility [1]. In animal studies it raises food intake mainly by increasing meal frequency [1]. It has also been linked to sleep cycles, glucose metabolism, reproduction, cardiovascular protection, immune regulation and stress responses [1].

Ghrelin becomes active when an octanoyl group is attached to its third serine residue by the enzyme ghrelin O-acyltransferase (GOAT) [1][6]. The desacyl form does not activate GHS-R1a but has other effects, and both forms occur in stomach tissue [1][7]. Ghrelin expression has also been found in the placenta and in human pituitary and neuroendocrine tumours [18][19].

Registered studies have examined ghrelin administration in cancer-related appetite loss (a phase 3 study of 30 patients and a phase 1/2 cachexia study of 21), frailty in ageing (5 participants), cystic fibrosis (20), stroke (80), peripheral artery disease with the unacylated form (25), alcohol craving (45), sleep and nocturnal hormone secretion (80), peripheral metabolic effects (8) and sympathetic nervous system effects in healthy volunteers and people with obesity (46) [3][4][5][11][12][20][21][22][23][24]. Results for these registrations are not summarised in the registry entries cited. Wikipedia states that evidence is insufficient to say whether ghrelin helps manage cachexia [1].

Observational and physiological work covers ghrelin response to bariatric surgery, with one study describing gut hormone profiles after surgery as favouring an anorectic state, and the endocrine consequences of anorexia nervosa [9][25]. No studies found of ghrelin administration for cosmetic or appearance goals.

Dietary and supplement trials sometimes record ghrelin as one of several outcomes; a 2024 meta-analysis of green tea extract trials included ghrelin among the obesity-related hormones it examined alongside body composition.[33]

Ghrelin was identified in 1999 after its receptor, GHS-R1a, had been found; the name reflects its growth-hormone-releasing activity [1]. A 2000 study characterised acylated and des-acyl forms in gastrointestinal tissue, and in 2008 the enzyme GOAT that attaches the octanoyl group was identified [6][7]. A synthetic ghrelin-receptor agonist developed at the University of Montpellier and CNRS in France, macimorelin, was approved by the FDA in December 2017 as an oral test for adult growth hormone deficiency, replacing injected stimulation tests [15]. The name comes from a root meaning to grow, reflecting its growth hormone-releasing activity.[1]
Related work includes the unacylated-ghrelin analogue livoletide, studied for hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome, and animal studies suggesting possible cardioprotective effects [1].

timeline.event: Ghrelin identified as the endogenous ligand of the GH secretagogue receptor.[1]
Acylated and des-acyl forms characterised in gastrointestinal tissue.[7]
Stomach ghrelin expression shown to rise with fasting; ghrelin also reported in placenta and pituitary tissue.[8][18][19]
Sleep curtailment in healthy young men linked to higher ghrelin and hunger.[17]
Ghrelin response after gastric bypass studied alongside other gut hormones.[9]
The enzyme GOAT, which octanoylates ghrelin, identified.[6]
Hormonal adaptations to weight loss reported to persist for a year.[10]
Macimorelin, a ghrelin-receptor agonist, approved by the FDA as a growth hormone deficiency diagnostic.[15]
Meta-analysis of 21 studies links short sleep with higher ghrelin.[13]
Randomised trial finds late eating increases hunger and decreases energy expenditure.[14]

lore.intro: Ghrelin is mentioned in fitness forums mostly as the 'hunger hormone': what raises it, which foods are said to quiet it, and which supplements mimic it.[26][27][30]

claims.claim: Eggs and protein-rich food lower ghrelin and keep hunger down
claims.believers: T Nation posters say eggs and fatty meats are very filling, and one quotes the idea that eggs suppress plasma ghrelin and so reduce appetite.[26]
claims.experts: Consumer-health reviewers say protein and fibre may lower ghrelin, citing individual studies; ghrelin is described in encyclopedias as appetite-stimulating, with levels falling after eating.[1][34]

claims.claim: Psyllium fibre controls ghrelin and peptide YY
claims.believers: A T Nation supplements thread says psyllium slows intestinal transit and enhances these hunger-controlling peptides.[27]
claims.experts: No trial of psyllium on ghrelin appears among the studies cited here.

claims.claim: Short sleep raises ghrelin and hunger, making dieting harder
claims.believers: Lifters and dieters describe poor sleep as increasing cravings.[34]
claims.experts: A randomised crossover study of 12 young men and a 2020 meta-analysis of 21 studies report higher ghrelin with short sleep.[13][17]

claims.claim: Weight loss raises ghrelin and hunger, so regain is hormonal
claims.believers: Dieters point to persistent hunger after losing weight as proof of a biological pushback.[10]
claims.experts: A 2011 NEJM study reported hormonal adaptations lasting a year; consumer-health coverage notes that ghrelin changes alone do not reliably predict regain.[10][34]

claims.believers: Meal-timing advocates avoid late meals to manage appetite.[14]
claims.experts: A randomised crossover trial in adults with overweight or obesity found late eating increased hunger and lowered energy expenditure with intake, activity, sleep and light held constant.[14]

claims.claim: Ghrelin-mimicking compounds build size and recovery by raising growth hormone
claims.believers: Forum users report strong hunger, water retention and fuller muscles in the first days on such products.[30][31]
claims.experts: Growth hormone secretagogues are mainly used clinically in growth hormone deficiency, and ghrelin administration has been studied in cachexia and other patient groups; no study tests them for appearance goals.[2][3][4][15]

claims.claim: GLP-1 drugs work partly by suppressing ghrelin, with rebound afterwards
claims.believers: A T Nation poster describes hormones rebounding to higher levels after stopping a GLP-1 drug.[28]
claims.experts: The cited research covers diets and bariatric surgery, where gut-hormone changes including ghrelin have been measured; GLP-1 rebound is not covered in these studies.[9][10]

card.summary: The stomach hunger hormone and GH secretagogue; central to appetite science, untested for looks.
card.note: Studied in cachexia and other clinical settings, not for cosmetic use.

quick.overview:
Ghrelin is the stomach hormone that signals hunger and also prompts growth hormone release. Its INN is lenomorelin.
It matters to body-composition discussion because appetite and growth hormone both affect fat and muscle, but no study has tested it for appearance goals.
quick.mechanism: Once an octanoyl group is attached by the enzyme GOAT, ghrelin activates the GHS-R1a receptor in the brain, pituitary and gut, driving hunger and growth hormone release.
quick.risks: Clinical use has been investigational, in conditions such as cancer cachexia. It is not an approved appearance treatment.

chain: Ghrelin rises before meals and with short sleep or fasting
Hunger and growth hormone release increase
Appetite and fat or lean mass are affected
angle.text: Ghrelin drives hunger and growth hormone release, so it shapes how easy it is to diet down or eat up. Its levels respond to sleep, meal timing and weight change, which is how it enters body-composition discussions.
